questions.question: Bobby's birthday is on Monday 5th June. On what day of the week will be Pinky's Birthday in the same year if Pinky was born on 22nd September?
questions.questionHtml: Bobby's birthday is on Monday 5th June. On what day of the week will be Pinky's Birthday in the same year if Pinky was born on 22nd September?
questions.solution:
Bobby’s birthday→ 5 June, Monday

Pinky’s birthday → 22 September

So, June has remaining → 25 Days

July → 31 Days

August → 31 Days

September → 22 Days

Total Days → 109 Days

Dividing 109 days by 7 (as there are 7 days in a week)

We get remainder 4

Thus, 4 days ahead of Bobby’s birthday will be Friday which is Pinky’s birthday.

Hence, the answer is Friday.

questions.question: __________ resources are those resources whose quantity is known.

questions.solution: Actual resources refer to those resources whose quantity is known and are being utilized. questions.question: Convex and concave mirrors are examples of?
questions.questionHtml: Convex and concave mirrors are examples of?
questions.solution:
• Convex and concave mirrors are examples of Spherical mirrors.
  • A spherical mirror is a kind of mirror that has been cut out of a spherical surface.

  • A concave mirror, or converging mirror, has a reflecting surface that is recessed inward (away from the incident light). Concave mirrors reflect light inward to one focal point. 

  • They are used to focus light. Unlike convex mirrors, concave mirrors show different image types depending on the distance between the object and the mirror.
  • These mirrors are called "converging mirrors" because they tend to collect light that falls on them, refocusing parallel incoming rays toward a focus. This is because the light is reflected at different angles at different spots on the mirror as the normal to the mirror surface differs at each spot.

  • A convex mirror or diverging mirror is a curved mirror in which the reflective surface bulges towards the light source.

  • Convex mirrors reflect light outwards, therefore they are not used to focus light. Such mirrors always form a virtual image, since the focal point (F) and the centre curvature (2F) are both imaginary points "inside" the mirror, that cannot be reached.

questions.question: A can paint a house in 25 days and B can do it in 10 days. Along with C, they did the job in 6.25 days only. Then in how many days, C alone can do the job?
questions.questionHtml: A can paint a house in 25 days and B can do it in 10 days. Along with C, they did the job in 6.25 days only. Then in how many days, C alone can do the job?
questions.solution:
A’s 1 day work = 1/25

B’s 1 day work = 1/10

Together with C, they do the job in 6.25 days,

⇒ A’s 1 day work + B’s 1 day work + C’s 1 day work = 1/6.25

⇒ 1/25 + 1/10 + C’s 1 day work = 4/25

⇒ C’s 1 day work = 4/25 – 7/50 = 1/50

∴ C can do the work alone in 50 days

questions.question: What is the area (in sq cm) of a regular hexagon of side 6 cm?
questions.questionHtml: What is the area (in sq cm) of a regular hexagon of side 6 cm?
questions.solution:
Given:

Side of regular hexagon = 6 cm

Formula used:

Area of a regular hexagon with side ‘a’ = 3√3/2 × a2

Calculation:

Area of regular hexagon with side 6 cm = 3√3/2 × 6 × 6 = 54√3 cm2

So, the area of a regular hexagon with side ‘6’ is 54√3 cm2

questions.question: If 1 saree is offered free on purchase of 3 sarees, what is the effective discount on each saree?
questions.questionHtml: If 1 saree is offered free on purchase of 3 sarees, what is the effective discount on each saree?
questions.solution:
Let marked price of 1 saree be Rs. x

Marked price of 4 sarees = 4x

Selling price of 4 sarees = Marked price of 3 sarees = 3x

Total discount = 4x – 3x = x

∴ Effective discount = (x/4x) × 100 = 25%

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of R and S is 6 : 7. Before 12 years the ratio of their ages was 9 : 11. What is R's present age (in years)?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of present ages of R and S is 6 : 7. Before 12 years the ratio of their ages was 9 : 11. What is R's present age (in years)?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of R and S be ‘6x’ and ‘7x’ years respectively

12 years ago, ratio of their ages = 9 ∶ 11

⇒ (6x – 12)/(7x – 12) = 9/11

⇒ 66x – 132 = 63x – 108

⇒ 66x – 63x = 132 – 108

⇒ 3x = 24

⇒ x = 24/3 = 8

∴ R’s present age = 6x = 6(8) = 48 years

questions.question: The average marks of 10 students in an examination was 25. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 34 instead of 43. What is the correct average?
questions.questionHtml: The average marks of 10 students in an examination was 25. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 34 instead of 43. What is the correct average?
questions.solution:
Total marks of 10 students before correction = 25 × 10 = 250

Total marks of 10 students after correction = 250 – 34 + 43 = 259

∴ Correct average = 259/10 = 25.9

questions.question: A wholesaler sells a jacket to a retailer at a profit of 25% and the retailer sells it to a customer at a profit of 20%. If the customer pays Rs. 2,400, what had it cost (in Rs.) the wholesaler ?
questions.questionHtml: A wholesaler sells a jacket to a retailer at a profit of 25% and the retailer sells it to a customer at a profit of 20%. If the customer pays Rs. 2,400, what had it cost (in Rs.) the wholesaler ?
questions.solution:
Let the cost of jacket to wholesaler be Rs. ‘x’

Profit of wholesaler = 25%

Cost to retailer = selling price of wholesaler = x + 25% of x = 1.25x

Profit of retailer = 20%

Cost to customer = selling price of retailer = 1.25x + 20% of 1.25x = 1.5x

⇒ 1.5x = 2400

⇒ x = 2400/1.5 = 1600

∴ Cost of jacket to wholesaler = Rs. 1600

questions.question: When a number is increased by 24, it becomes 104% of itself. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: When a number is increased by 24, it becomes 104% of itself. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be ‘x’

⇒ x + 24 = 104% of x

⇒ x + 24 = 1.04x

⇒ 0.04x = 24

⇒ x = 24/0.04 = 600

∴ The number is 600

questions.question: If a boat goes a certain distance at 30 km/h and comes back the same distance at 20 km/hr, what is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey ?
questions.questionHtml: If a boat goes a certain distance at 30 km/h and comes back the same distance at 20 km/hr, what is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey ?
questions.solution:
When equal distance is travelled with different speeds of ‘x’ km/hr and ‘y’ km/hr, then,

Average speed = 2xy/(x + y)

Given, speeds of 30 km/hr and 20 km/hr,

∴ Average speed of journey = (2 × 30 × 20)/(30 + 20) = 1200/50 = 24 km/hr

questions.question: A sum fetched a total simple interest of Rs. 1200 at the rate of 7.5%/yr in 4 years. What is the sum (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: A sum fetched a total simple interest of Rs. 1200 at the rate of 7.5%/yr in 4 years. What is the sum (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given, SI = Rs. 1200, Rate = 7.5%, Time = 4 years

∵ Simple interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

⇒ 1200 = (Principal × 7.5 × 4)/100

∴ Principal sum of money = 120000/30 = Rs. 4000

questions.question: If a + b = 3 and ab = -4, then what is the value of a 3 + b 3 ?
questions.questionHtml: If a + b = 3 and ab = -4, then what is the value of a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup>?
questions.solution:
Given:

a + b = 3 

ab = -4 

Concept used:

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 – 3ab(a + b)

Calculations:

a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 - 3ab(a + b)

⇒ a3 + b3 = (3)3 - 3(-4)(3)

⇒ 27 + 36 = 63

∴ a3 + b3 is 63

questions.question: The sum of a non-zero number and 9 times its reciprocal is 10. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of a non-zero number and 9 times its reciprocal is 10. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be ‘x’

⇒ x + 9/x = 10

⇒ x2 + 9 = 10x

⇒ x2 – 10x + 9 = 0

⇒ x2 – 9x – x + 9 = 0

⇒ x(x – 9) – 1(x – 9) = 0

⇒ (x – 9)(x – 1) = 0

⇒ x = 9, 1

∴ The number is 9

questions.question: If the 1 st and the 3 rd term of an arithmetic progression are -10 and -4, what is the 12 th term?
questions.questionHtml: If the 1<sup>st</sup> and the 3<sup>rd</sup> term of an arithmetic progression are -10 and -4, what is the 12<sup>th </sup>term?
questions.solution:
The nth term of an AP with first term ‘a’ and difference ‘d’ = a + (n - 1)d

1st term = a = -10

3rd term = a + 2d = -4

⇒ -10 + 2d = -4

⇒ 2d = 10 - 4 = 6

⇒ d = 3

∴ 12th term = a + 11d = -10 + 11(3) = -10 + 33 = 23

questions.question: Point A divides segment BC in the ratio 1 : 3. The co-ordinates of B are (4, -4) and that of C are (0, 6). What are the co-ordinates of point A?
questions.questionHtml: Point A divides segment BC in the ratio 1 : 3. The co-ordinates of B are (4, -4) and that of C are (0, 6). What are the co-ordinates of point A?
questions.solution:
According to the section formula, if a point A(x, y) that lies on a line segment BC joining points B(x1, y1) and C(x2, y2), divides the line in the ratio m∶ n, then the coordinates of A can be computed as,

Coordinates of A = (x, y) = [(mx2 + nx1)/(m + n)], [(my2 + ny1)/(m + n)]

Given, point A divides the segment joining B(4, -4) and C(0, 6) in the ratio 1 ∶ 3

Hence,

X – coordinate of A = (0 + 12)/(1 + 3) = 12/4 = 3

Y – coordinate of A = (6 - 12)/(1 + 3) = -6/4 = -1.5

∴ Coordinates of A = (3, -1.5)

questions.question: What is the slope of the line parallel to the line passing through the points (-2, -1) and (4, -3)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the slope of the line parallel to the line passing through the points (-2, -1) and (4, -3)?
questions.solution:
Given:

points (-2, -1) and (4, -3)

Concept used:

The slope ‘m’ of the line passing through two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is computed as,

m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)

Calculation:

Slope of line passing through the points = (-3 + 1)/(4 + 2) = -2/6 = -1/3

∵ slope of parallel lines is equal,

So, the slope of required line = -1/3

questions.question: ΔXYZ is similar to ΔPQR. If ratio of perimeters of ΔXYZ : ΔPQR is 3 : 2 and if PQ = 6 cm then what is the length of XY (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: ΔXYZ is similar to ΔPQR. If ratio of perimeters of ΔXYZ : ΔPQR is 3 : 2 and if PQ = 6 cm then what is the length of XY (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔXYZ ~ ΔPQR

ΔXYZ : ΔPQR = 3 : 2

PQ = 6 cm

Concept used:

The ratio of the perimeters of similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides

Calculation:

perimeter(ΔXYZ)/perimeter(ΔPQR) = XY/PQ

⇒ 3/2 = XY/6

⇒ XY = (3 × 6)/2 = 9 cm

∴ Length of XY = 9 cm

So, the length of XY = 9 cm

questions.question: Sec 45° + Tan 30° = ?
questions.questionHtml: Sec 45° + Tan 30° = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

sec 45° + tan 30°

Calculation:

sec 45° + tan 30°

⇒ 1/cos 45° + tan 30°

⇒ √2 + 1/√3            (∵ cos 45° = 1/√2, tan 30° = 1/√3)

⇒ (√6 + 1)/√3

So, the value of sec 45° + tan 30° is (√6 + 1)/√3

questions.question: ΔDEF is right angled at E. If ∠D = 45°, then Cosec F = ?
questions.questionHtml: ΔDEF is right angled at E. If ∠D = 45°, then Cosec F = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

∆DEF is right-angled at E

∠E = 90° , ∠D = 45°

Concept used:

Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

Calculation:

Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

∠D + ∠E + ∠F = 180°

⇒ 45° + 90° + ∠F = 180°

⇒ ∠F = 180° – 135° = 45°

∴ cosec F = cosec 45° = √2

So, the value of cosec F is √2

questions.question: If cos θ = 5/13, then cosec θ = ?
questions.questionHtml: If cos θ = 5/13, then cosec θ = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

cosθ = 5/13

Formula used:

sin2 θ = 1 – cos2 θ

cosec θ = 1/sin θ

Calculation:

sin2 θ = 1 – cos2 θ = 1 - (5/13)2 = 144/169

⇒ sin θ = √(144/169) = 12/13

∴ cosec θ = 1/sin θ = 1/(12/13) = 13/12

So, the value of cosec θ = 13/12

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. Whine
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.

Whine
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Gripe.

Key Points

  • The word "Whine" means to complain in a feeble or petulant way. (किरकिराना/शिकायत करना)
    • Example: She tends to whine about minor inconveniences.
  • Gripe means to complain about something in a persistent, nagging manner. (शिकायत करना)
    • Example: He often gripes about the long hours at work.
  • Hence, to whine and to gripe both refer to complaining, making them similar in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Gripe.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Gratification (संतोष): Pleasure or satisfaction gained from something.
    • Example: She felt immense gratification after completing the project successfully.
  • Luxury (विलासिता): A state of great comfort or elegance, especially when involving great expense.
    • Example: They enjoyed the luxury of staying in a five-star hotel.
  • Thrill (रोमांच): A sudden feeling of excitement and pleasure.
    • Example: The thrill of the roller coaster ride was electrifying.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. Requisite
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.

Requisite
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Precondition.

Key Points

  • The word "Requisite" means something that is necessary or required for a particular purpose. (आवश्यक)
    • Example: Having a passport is a requisite for international travel.
  • "Precondition" refers to a condition that must be fulfilled before other things can happen or be done. (पूर्वशर्त)
    • Example: Passing the entrance exam is a precondition for being admitted to the university.
  • Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to 'Requisite' is 'Precondition'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Precondition.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Peripheral (परिधीय): Relating to or situated on the edge or periphery of something.
    • Example: The company's peripheral activities are being outsourced.
  • Deadwood (बेकार लोग या चीजें): People or things that are no longer useful or productive.
    • Example: The manager decided to cut the deadwood from the team.
  • Trivial (तुच्छ): Of little value or importance.
    • Example: She often spends her time on trivial matters.

Y -sand, thoroughly tired out, and

Z -ourselves down on the
questions.solution:
Ans: ZYX

Sol: Z is the first sentence as it continues the ‘flung’ part with ‘ourselves down’. Y comes next as it continues the ‘down on the’ part with the ‘sand’. Hence, ZYX is the correct combination of sentences, which is seen only in Option 4, making it the right choice.
